papers.abstract: Bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) is a severe complication of antiresorptive therapy with poorly understood vascular mechanisms. Here, we integrate whole-organ tissue-clearing imaging, single-cell transcriptomics, and proteomics to construct a multimodal atlas of the mouse and human BRONJ mandibular microenvironment. We identify gross vascular and lymphatic rarefaction and four endothelial subtypes with aberrant Col2a1 upregulation. Fibroblasts and macrophages emerge as key endothelial interactors, highlighting dysregulation of the endothelium-matrix-immune axis. Unlike homeostatic Dmp1⁺/Tfap2a⁺ fibroblasts and Stab1⁺ macrophages, BRONJ lesions feature pathological Lrrc15⁺/Chad⁺ fibroblasts and Il6⁺ macrophages, driving ectopic chondrogenesis and inflammation. Mechanistically, the COL2A1-CD44 axis (EC-to-fibroblast/macrophage signaling) and COL2A1-SDC4 axis (EC-to-fibroblast signaling) are upregulated in BRONJ disease condition, while lineage tracing excludes EndoMT, implicating extracellular matrix remodeling. We functionally validate this axis via localized Col2a1 siRNA silencing and endothelial-specific genetic deletion. Cross-species validation in human mandibles confirms vascular-lymphatic dysregulation, inflammation, and chondrogenesis. Overall, we establish vascular and lymphatic dysregulation as a BRONJ hallmark and identify the COL2A1-CD44/SDC4 axis as a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Among patient with early-stage breast cancer, breast conservation surgery (BCS) is the most performed surgery, utilized in approximately two-thirds of patients. While 5-year overall-survival rates are strong-typically above 90%-additional re-excisions can occur in up to 25% of patients who undergo index BCS and some patients will require subsequent surgery for new breast cancer or recurrences. As such, these additional procedures can complicate patients' pathway to survivorship, negatively impact quality of life, and lead to excess healthcare costs. This retrospective cohort study used linked claims and an electronic healthcare record database to (1) characterize patients at higher risk for additional breast oncologic surgery (aBOS) following BCS, and (2) quantify the long-term financial impact of aBOS after BCS. In total, 87,190 patients with breast cancer, who had an index BCS between January 1, 2012, to March 31, 2023, were followed for up to 5-years post-operatively. Patients with and without aBOS were analyzed, comparing demographics, tumor characteristics, healthcare utilization, and per-person-per-month (PPPM) costs. Twenty-three percent (n = 20,212) of patients underwent aBOS. These patients were younger, had higher tumor grades and larger tumor sizes, and incurred greater healthcare costs compared to patients who did not undergo a secondary surgery. This study highlights significant factors influencing BCS outcomes and healthcare utilization, underscoring the need for tailored therapeutic strategies for patients with breast cancer.

papers.abstract: To compare proton dynamic arc therapy (DynamicArc) with conventional intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) for breast/chest wall irradiation across diverse clinical anatomies. Forty patients were analyzed (10/cohort): tissue expanders, permanent implants, no reconstruction, and bilateral disease. DynamicArc plans used coplanar partial arcs (150-160°) with arc retracing; paired IMPT plans used 2-4 static fields. RayStation 2023BDTK-generated plans shared contours and prescriptions (50.4 Gy[RBE]/28; subset bilateral 42.56 Gy[RBE]/16) and were robustly optimized/evaluated (±5 mm setup,±3.5% range) with Monte Carlo dose calculation (0.5%uncertainty,40000ions/spot) and a 7.5cm range shifter. Target coverage and OAR endpoints were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with FDR correction. Additionally, robustness pass rates, LETd metrics, and estimated treatment times were compared. DynamicArc achieved target coverage comparable to IMPT and improved robustness pass rates for selected targets. In the expander cohort, DynamicArc improved coverage posterior to the expander port and increased coverage of the chest wall evaluation volume and nodal targets. Improved D95% was accompanied by increased target V105% in several targets. DynamicArc increased thyroid mean dose and skin V95% in multiple cohorts, although skin D2cc and skin V100% remained low. Focal hotspot metrics for the esophagus, heart, and LAD were largely unchanged, with LAD D0.03cc numerically lower though not statistically significant in the expander cohort. Ipsilateral lung V20 was generally similar, with a reduction in implant cases. Several unadjusted significant findings did not remain significant after FDR correction. High-dose CTV LETd was broadly comparable between techniques with changes in the tails of the distribution. DynamicArc increased spots, energy layers, and beam-on time, but estimated total treatment time was comparable after accounting for IMPT room entry and imaging. DynamicArc achieved comparable target coverage with improved robustness in challenging anatomies, at the cost of increased V105%, thyroid mean dose, and skin V95% while maintaining comparable treatment times.

papers.abstract: Abstract CD24 is highly expressed in aggressive B-cell malignancies and represents a novel immunologic vulnerability to overcome resistance to CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. We developed a CD24 × CD3 bispecific antibody (CD24 BsAb) and CXCR3-armed CD24 CAR-T cells, both exhibiting potent antitumor activity in lymphoma and leukemia models. CD24 BsAb and CD24 CAR-T overcome CD19 CAR-T resistance driven by antigen loss and apoptosis defects in vitro and in vivo. Beyond direct cytotoxicity, CD24-targeted T cells reprogram macrophages toward an M1-like phenotype and enhance phagocytic clearance. We further engineered a dual-specific, dual-functional CD19 CAR-T that secretes a CD24 bispecific T-cell engager (CD24 BiTE), enabling simultaneous targeting of CD19 and CD24 to address tumor heterogeneity and achieve superior efficacy. Collectively, our study demonstrates that CD24-directed adoptive T-cell therapies are warranted for B-cell malignancies through robust induction of both innate and adaptive immune responses.

papers.abstract: Routine blood counts may capture treatment-related host immune perturbation in glioblastoma, but most studies rely on static pretreatment values. We investigated whether the intra-individual preservation of circulating monocytes during chemoradiotherapy provides prognostic information beyond established clinical factors and other hematologic trajectories. We retrospectively analyzed adults with histologically confirmed IDH-wildtype glioblastoma treated with radiotherapy and concurrent temozolomide. Absolute monocyte counts obtained before and at the end of chemoradiotherapy were used to define monocytic resilience as log2(post-treatment/pre-treatment monocyte ratio). Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint. Cox models adjusted for MGMT promoter methylation, gross total resection, Karnofsky Performance Status, and age. The ratio was analyzed continuously for primary inference. A post/pre ratio of 0.75 was additionally evaluated as an exploratory, clinically interpretable threshold for two-group Kaplan-Meier visualization and sensitivity analysis. Among 127 patients, 115 had complete monocyte trajectories and OS data. The primary adjusted model included 102 patients and 86 deaths. The continuous monocyte post/pre ratio was independently associated with OS (HR 0.53 per doubling, 95% CI 0.37-0.76; p = 0.00051). Using the exploratory 0.75 threshold, 52 patients had low resilience (< 0.75) and 63 had preserved resilience (≥ 0.75), with median OS of 10.2 and 17.3 months, respectively (log-rank p = 0.00064). Preserved resilience was associated with lower mortality in univariable Cox analysis (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.34-0.75; p = 0.00080). Bootstrap resampling showed that outcome-optimized cut-points clustered around this region (median 0.74; IQR 0.70-0.81), although the threshold remains exploratory and requires external validation. Preservation or recovery of circulating monocytes during chemoradiotherapy was associated with a favorable host-response phenotype in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. This dynamic signal remained associated with survival after adjustment for established clinical factors, baseline monocyte burden, lymphocyte change, systemic inflammatory imbalance, and measured corticosteroid exposure. External prospective validation, medication-level confounder assessment, and immune phenotyping are required before clinical use.

papers.abstract: To characterize the weekly trajectory of hippocampal diffusion during fractionated partial-brain radiation therapy (RT) for high-grade glioma and determine whether the magnitude of change is associated with planned hippocampal dose. Forty-five adults enrolled in a prospective observational imaging study and treated with 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concurrent temozolomide underwent diffusion MRI before RT and weekly during treatment. Relative bilateral hippocampal apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) change and fractional anisotropy (FA) were evaluated longitudinally. Linear mixed-effects models included treatment week and planned mean bilateral hippocampal dose as fixed main effects. A secondary laterally-specific analysis evaluated baseline-to-Week-6 ADC change separately in the hippocampi ipsilateral and contralateral to the tumor. Hippocampal ADC increased progressively from a median relative change of 0.5% at Week 1 to 12% (IQR, 6%-18%) at Week 6. The ADC time coefficient was + 2.2% points per week (95% CI, 1.8-2.5; P < 0.001). After accounting for week, higher planned mean bilateral hippocampal dose was associated with greater ADC change (+ 0.81% points/Gy; 95% CI, 0.76-0.93; P < 0.001). In the secondary laterally-specific analysis, higher dose was associated with greater Week-6 ADC change in both the ipsilateral hippocampus (β = 0.83% points/Gy; 95% CI, 0.52-1.26; P = 0.013) and the contralateral hippocampus (β = 0.36% points/Gy; 95% CI, 0.05-0.712; P = 0.046). FA remained stable through Week 3 and declined during Weeks 4-6. Weekly diffusion MRI demonstrates a progressive, dose-associated hippocampal response during fractionated RT. The laterality-specific findings further support an association between local radiation exposure and ADC change and support hippocampal ADC as a candidate treatment-phase imaging phenotype for prospective validation.

papers.abstract: High-dose hyper-fractionated radiotherapy has been recently included in NCCN guidelines for limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), which clinical outcomes are dependent on actually delivered biologically effective dose (BED). However, most tumor control probability (TCP) and normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models rely on planed physical dose without considering inter-fractional deviations and BED of fractionization. This study aims to develop TCP and NTCP models for LS-SCLC incorporating CBCT-based inter-fractional anatomies and hyper-fractional radiobiological dose. Inter-fractional dose was accumulated based on deformable image registration between CBCT and planning CT (pCT). Both TCP and NTCP were formulated within a BED-based framework, using dose-volume parameters calculated from planned dose and CBCT-based accumulated dose for comparison. The LQ model with "4R" effects and Gompertzian tumor growth (LQRG) and Lyman-Kutcher-Burman (LKB) models were used for TCP and NTCP modeling. Based on the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), negative log-likelihood (NLL), and Akaike information criterion (AIC), model performances were assessed for local progression-free survival (LPFS), radiation pneumonitis and radiation esophagitis. Compared with pCT dose, CBCT dose showed superior discrimination of normal tissue toxicity. For grade ≥2 radiation pneumonitis, the CBCT-based NTCP model achieved significantly higher AUC (0.67 vs. 0.59) and lower NLL (62.39 vs. 66.13) than that of the pCT-based mode. Superiority of CBCT-based NTCP model was also observed for grade ≥3 radiation esophagitis, i.e., AUC (0.62 vs. 0.58) and NLL (55.55 vs. 56.64). Using the observed LPFS as reference, marginally improved TCP modeling was observed using CBCT dose than that of pCT, where the AUC values were 0.80 vs. 0.79 (GTV 45 Gy) and 0.77 vs. 0.75 (GTV 54 Gy). By incorporating inter-fractional deviation and biological effectiveness, the improved accuracy of TCP and NTCP models provides preliminary evidence supporting the treatment planning and toxicity management for LS-SCLC patients treated with the hyper-fractionated radiotherapy, which needs further clinical validation.

papers.abstract: Despite significant advances in glioma surgery, early postoperative neuroimaging frequently reveals signs of surgical brain injury (SBI). This prospective observational study aimed to investigate the incidence, radiological characteristics, neurological outcomes and risk factors of SBI following glioma resection. Patients with newly diagnosed supratentorial gliomas who undergo tumor resection were prospectively enrolled. Serial MRI examinations were administrated early postoperative (≤ 72 h) and on postoperative days 7, 14 and 28 to assess the characteristics of infarction, edema and microhemorrhage. Neurological outcomes were evaluated using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at postoperative day 28. A total of 64 patients was included. Postoperative infarction was identified in 14 patients (21.9%), with all anatomically localized to the basal ganglia, thalamus, or insular regions. Intraoperative blood loss ≥ 300 mL was independently associated with postoperative infarction (Odd Ratio [OR]: 4.62, p = 0.035). Microhemorrhage was observed in 53.8% of patients. Peritumoral edema occurred in all cases and exhibited two distinct patterns: residual tumor-associated edema (n = 42) and de novo surgery-induced edema (n = 22). The average volume of tumor-associated edema decreased, whereas that of surgery-induced edema increased over time. Among the 53 patients who completed neurological outcome assessments, 13 developed disability (mRS ≥ 2). Risk factors were higher intraoperative blood loss (OR: 8.88, p = 0.013) and postoperative infarction (OR: 6.33, p = 0.031). SBI, including infarction and edema, is common following glioma surgery and associated with adverse neurological outcomes. Meticulous intraoperative hemostatic management is essential to prevent postoperative infarction and even disability outcome.

papers.abstract: Timely medical intervention is critical to achieve optimal outcomes in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, yet numerous patients experience delayed or forgone (D/F) medical care. This study aimed to evaluate the national impact of D/F care on emergency surgical interventions and associated healthcare expenditures among patients with GI cancers. Adults with a self-reported history of GI cancer were identified from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, 2007-2017. Multivariable regression analyzes was performed to assess associations between D/F medical care, ED-associated GI surgery, inpatient utilization, and related healthcare expenditures after adjusting for demographic and socioeconomic variables. Among a weighted sample of 6 517 883 patients with GI cancers, 8.5% (n = 552 751) reported D/F medical care. Patients with D/F care were older (76 years [IQR: 69-82] vs. 68 years [IQR: 58-76]), more frequently male (57.3% vs. 50.6%) and frequently had family income below the poverty line (40.2% vs. 11.3%) (all p < 0.001). Furthermore, individuals reporting D/F care were more likely to have emergency department visits (44.2% vs. 27.4%), hospitalizations (64.6% vs. 34.5%) (both p < 0.05), or undergo ED-associated GI surgery (41.0% vs. 19.1%; p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, after adjusting for relevant factors, D/F care was associated with markedly greater odds of ED-associated GI surgery (OR 2.70, 95%CI 1.47-4.95) and higher annual inpatient healthcare costs (β +$31,410, 95% CI $23,592-$39,227) compared with individuals who did not report D/F care. Self-reported D/F medical care was associated with greater acute healthcare utilization, higher odds of ED-associated GI surgery, and greater healthcare expenditures. These findings highlight the importance of understanding barriers to healthcare access among adults with a history of GI cancer.

papers.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) tumors pose a major global health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where outcomes remain disproportionately poor. The global CONCORD-3 study (Lancet Oncology) highlighted stark disparities in five-year survival (2010-2014): from ∼15% in Thailand to 46% in Japan among adults, and from ∼ 80% in Denmark to < 40% in Brazil among children. Limited access to specialized pathology and molecular diagnostics in LMICs results in diagnostic uncertainty and restricted treatment options. DNA methylation-based tumor classification, has revolutionized CNS tumor diagnosis and got incorporated into the 2021 world health organization (WHO) CNS5 classification. However, its accessibility, feasibility, and performance in LMICs remain insufficiently explored. Importantly, several ethnic groups common in LMICs are underrepresented in current reference datasets. To address this, the Molecular Neuro-Pathology (MNP) Outreach Consortium was launched in Heidelberg, partnering with 11 countries-including nine LMICs from Asia, Africa, and South America. Early insights from Brazil, Jordan and Argentina, show methylation profiling changing diagnosis in up to 25% cases. Gains are greatest in pediatric and adolescents and young adults (AYA) populations. In addition, it reduced the designation of not otherwise specified (NOS) from 51.3% to 8.8% across 476 CNS tumours in Brazil.

papers.abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality. 2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height)2.7(LVMI g/m2.7) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores. LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m2.7, ≥ 91 g/m2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death. LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

papers.abstract: Germline DDX41 variants are a recognized cause of adult myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS), characterized by distinct biological features and favorable prognosis. The independent effect of DDX41 status on outcomes after allogeneic transplantation, the role of conditioning intensity, and treatment-related toxicity risk remain unresolved. To address this gap, we analyzed 1,514 patients with MDS undergoing transplantation prior to routine DDX41 testing alongside a wild-type comparator, providing an unbiased benchmark for this molecular subgroup. Forty-nine patients (3.2%) carried pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) germline DDX41 variants; 19 (39%) had an additional somatic DDX41 mutation, most commonly p.R525H. P/LP DDX41 cases were older (median 63 vs 59 years) and showed lower IPSS-M risk with absent TP53 mutations (0% vs 21%). In terms of outcome, 2-year relapse incidence was significantly lower in P/LP DDX41 (17% vs 34%, p=0.01). In multivariable analysis, the presence of a DDX41 P/LP variant independently associated with lower risk of relapse (hazard ratio 0.43, 95% CI 0.21-0.88; p=0.02), concentrated in the reduced-intensity/nonmyeloablative stratum. Adjusted models showed significantly improved disease-free survival (DFS) for P/LP DDX41 (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.41-0.95; p=0.03) and no significant association with non-relapse mortality (NRM) or graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). In summary, these findings identify DDX41-associated MDS as a transplant subgroup with superior DFS regardless of conditioning intensity driven by reduced relapse risk and lack of excess NRM and GVHD supporting incorporation of germline DDX41 status into transplant planning.

papers.abstract: Reduced-port surgery has been developed to minimize abdominal wall trauma while maintaining the benefits of minimally invasive surgery. However, reduced-port robotic rectal surgery remains technically challenging due to interference of external arms. The modular design of the Hugo RAS system (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) provides greater flexibility in arm positioning to minimize external arm interference without compromising instrument maneuverability1-4. In abdominoperineal resection (APR), the incision for a permanent colostomy is inevitable. We report the first case of completely robot-assisted APR performed using the Hugo RAS system through a planned stoma site. Three robotic trocars were inserted through the planned left lower-quadrant stoma site, and one arm through the right lower quadrant. We call this approach SIPORS, Single-Incision Plus One Robot-assisted Surgery. The procedure is presented in the accompanying video. As the first case, a 50-year-old woman with rectal cancer underwent APR after systemic chemotherapy. The console time was 167 min. The procedure was completed without significant robotic arm interference. The postoperative course was uneventful except for transient cystitis. The circumferential and distal resection margins were 3 and 35 mm, respectively. The mesorectal specimen was complete, 25 lymph nodes were harvested, and the pathological stage was pT3N2bM1. SIPORS using the Hugo RAS at a planned stoma site was technically feasible and achieved an oncologically acceptable resection in this patient. It may offer improved cosmesis, reduced postoperative pain, fewer wound complications, and a lower risk of trocar-site incisional hernia. Further experience is needed to confirm its reproducibility and clinical benefits.

papers.abstract: Reliable biomarkers for predicting tumor aggressiveness and pathological upstaging in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remain limited. DR-70, a biomarker reflecting circulating fibrin and fibrin degradation products, has been associated with tumor progression in several malignancies. This study aimed to investigate the association between preoperative serum DR-70 levels and pathological stage and nuclear grade in patients with localized RCC. This prospective single-center study included 69 patients who underwent partial or radical nephrectomy for localized RCC. Tumors were staged according to the TNM classification and graded using the World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology system. Preoperative serum DR-70 levels were measured, and their associations with clinical stage, pathological stage, and nuclear grade were evaluated. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of pathological upstaging (≥ pT3). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to assess the predictive performance of DR-70. The median serum DR-70 level was 0.84 U/mL. DR-70 levels were significantly higher in high-grade tumors than in low-grade tumors (1.32 vs. 0.78 U/mL, p = 0.001). No significant association was observed between DR-70 levels and clinical stage (p = 0.53), whereas a significant association was found with pathological stage (p = 0.023). Multivariate analysis identified serum DR-70 as an independent predictor of pathological upstaging (≥ pT3) (odds ratio 1.40; 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.81; p = 0.008). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated good predictive performance for high-grade disease (area under the curve 0.823) and pathological upstaging (area under the curve 0.774), with an optimal cutoff value of 1.02 U/mL. Serum DR-70 was associated with tumor aggressiveness and independently predicted pathological upstaging in patients with localized RCC. These findings suggest that DR-70 may serve as a complementary biomarker for preoperative risk stratification and may help identify patients at increased risk of aggressive pathological features. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) activity and target-dependent on-target/off-tumor toxicity depends in part on which cells express the target antigen, a feature that bulk assays cannot resolve. We analyzed a publicly available whole-transcriptome CosMx breast tumor dataset including 154,816 cells and 18,934 genes. Eleven clinically relevant ADC targets were profiled across seven annotated lineages. Findings were contextualized using TCGA-BRCA bulk transcriptomes (1,097 tumors and 114 normal tissues) and assessed in two public Xenium breast cancer specimens. HER2 (ERBB2), TROP2 (TACSTD2), HER3 (ERBB3), NECTIN4 and MUC1 were enriched in tumor epithelium. B7-H3 (CD276) was highest in endothelial and myoepithelial cells, with similar mean expression in stromal and tumor cells. PSMA (FOLH1) was enriched in endothelium. TCGA-BRCA tumor-normal differences did not identify these cellular sources. No overall-survival association remained after multiple-testing correction or covariate adjustment. HER2 and TROP2 tumor enrichment recurred in both Xenium specimens, whereas EGFR was not tumor restricted. Cell-resolved spatial profiling separated ADC targets enriched in tumor epithelium from those expressed in vascular and stromal compartments. B7-H3 and PSMA localization was consistent with prior immunohistochemical reports and is confirmatory. These RNA-level results do not establish surface-protein abundance, ADC response, or clinical toxicity. Low-abundance microenvironmental findings remain based on a single discovery specimen and require protein-level validation. Protein-level confirmation, and correlation with ADC efficacy and toxicity, are required before these maps can inform clinical decisions.

papers.abstract: Experimental studies suggest that thyroid hormones may influence tumor development through endocrine and cellular signaling pathways. Although malignant melanoma (MM) is primarily associated with ultraviolet radiation exposure, the potential role of thyroid dysfunction in melanoma development remains unclear. We investigated the association between hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism and the rate of MM in a nationwide cohort of Danish women. Our cohort comprised 1,058,939 women born between January 1, 1960, and December 31, 1997, and was followed from 1996 to 2022. Information on thyroid disease, MM diagnoses, covariates and follow-up was obtained from Danish nationwide registries. Cox proportional hazards models with attained age as the underlying scale were used to estimate Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Analyses were stratified by time since diagnosis, menopausal status and histological subtype. Hyperthyroidism was not associated with the rate of overall MM (HR: 0.94; 95% CI: 0.79-1.12). For hypothyroidism, the HR for overall MM was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.77-1.02). Estimates for superficial spreading MM were similar. Among women diagnosed with hypothyroidism within the past 10 years, the HR for superficial spreading MM was 0.80 (95% CI: 0.66-0.98). Stratification by menopausal status did not materially alter the associations. Our findings do not provide clear evidence of an association between thyroid dysfunction and the rate of MM in women. The observed decreased rate of superficial spreading MM among women with hypothyroidism within 10 years of diagnosis should be interpreted cautiously, as it was the only statistically significant finding among multiple subgroup analyses and may represent a chance finding. Further studies incorporating detailed clinical and biochemical measures of thyroid function are warranted.

papers.abstract: Primary breast angiosarcoma (PBA) is rare, and limited data exist because studies often combine primary and secondary angiosarcoma patients. For patients with PBA who received care at a comprehensive cancer center from 1991 to 2025 and underwent surgical resection, this retrospective study collected and analyzed clinicopathologic features, treatment patterns, and survival data. Among 176 patients, 138 met the inclusion criteria. The median age was 40 years (interquartile range [IQR], 32-49 years). Most of the tumors were high grade with a median size of 6.5 cm. Most of the patients underwent mastectomy (88%). Among the 50 patients (36%) who underwent axillary surgery, only 6 patients had nodal metastases. Multimodal treatment was performed for 121 patients (88%), including chemotherapy/surgery (n = 46, 38%), radiation therapy (RT)/surgery ( = 15, 12%), and chemotherapy/RT/surgery (n = 60, 50%). The median follow-up time was 3.7 years. The median overall survival (OS) was 6 years (IQR, 3.5-8.7 years), and the 5-year OS was 58%. Recurrence was experienced by 62% of the patients, with a median recurrence-free survival (RFS) of 3 years (IQR, 1.4-7.7 years). Most of the recurrences were distant (79%), with 14% of the patients experiencing local recurrence only. Tumor size larger than 5 cm and high-grade histology were independently associated with lower OS. When stratified by treatment modality, there was no statistical difference in OS (p = 0.475). Primary breast angiosarcoma arises in women with a median age of 40 years, and large, high-grade tumors are associated with worse survival outcomes. Distant recurrence is common, whereas nodal metastases and local failure are not. Most of the patients in this study received multimodal therapy without a clear impact of modality on OS. However, further collaborative studies may be required to assess the impact of modality on disease outcomes.

papers.abstract: Staging laparoscopy (SL) is a minimally invasive approach for detecting occult metastases in patients with pancreatic cancer (PC) without signs of metastasis on imaging. This study aimed to identify the predictive factors for imaging-negative occult metastases. This prospective study enrolled 199 patients with histologically confirmed PC from three institutions between August 2021 and April 2023. All patients were scheduled for a treatment plan that included SL. The overall metastasis rate as detected using SL was 25.1%, which varied from 20.6% in patients with resectable PC (R-PC) to 33.8% in those with borderline resectable or locally advanced unresectable PC (BR/URLA-PC). In 152 patients who did not receive neoadjuvant therapy, BR/URLA status (odds ratio 3.261; 95% confidence interval 1.185-9.483, p = 0.022) and pancreatic body/tail lesions (odds ratio 2.653; 95% confidence interval 1.037-7.214, p = 0.042) were independent risk factors for occult metastatic lesions (M1). Among the 107 patients with R-PC, M1 disease was significantly associated with pancreatic body/tail lesions, tumor size, and elevated levels of tumor markers. In particular, elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels were consistent across all patients with M1 pancreatic head cancer. In contrast, no statistical differences were observed for any of these factors in the 45 patients with BR/URLA-PC. Our findings support the importance of SL in patients with BR/UR PC. For R-PC, patients with pancreatic head lesions and normal tumor marker values may represent a very low-risk subgroup where selective omission of SL can be considered in resource-constrained settings.

papers.abstract: Conventional survival analyses cannot fully account for recurrence as an intermediate event that dynamically influences subsequent mortality. Multistate models (MSMs) enable explicit modeling of transitions between clinically relevant disease states; however, their application among patients undergoing resection for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remains limited. An international multi-institutional database was queried to identify patients undergoing curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLM between 1998 and 2023. A four-state MSM was constructed comprising alive and recurrence-free, alive with recurrence, colorectal cancer (CRC)-related death, and non-CRC-related death. Transition probabilities and transition-specific prognostic factors were evaluated RESULTS: Among 3002 patients, 1624 (54.1%) developed recurrence and 911 (56.1%) died, predominantly from CRC-related causes (92.8%). The probability of recurrence decreased substantially the longer patients remained recurrence-free after surgery, whereas recurrence markedly worsened subsequent prognosis. High tumor burden score was independently associated with transition to recurrence (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06 per unit; 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.08; p < 0.001) but not post-recurrence mortality, suggesting that the adverse prognostic impact of tumor burden was mediated primarily through recurrence. Adjuvant chemotherapy reduced recurrence (HR 0.76; p = 0.005) and CRC-related death from the recurrence-free state (HR 0.39; p = 0.002). MSMs provide a dynamic framework to characterize disease evolution after CRLM resection and represent recurrence as a clinically meaningful time-dependent intermediate state rather than a simple binary endpoint. Recurrence was the dominant determinant of long-term prognosis, supporting the role of MSMs for individualized prognostication and surveillance after hepatectomy for CRLM.

papers.abstract: Evidence for exocomets has been found in PDS 70, a young planetary system where planets are still forming. The discovery extends exocomet studies into an earlier stage of planetary evolution, when planets, planetesimals and protoplanetary discs coexist.
